name: Florence
operatingHours: Tramvia lines T1 (Villa Costanza–Santa Maria Novella–Careggi) and T2 (Airport–Santa Maria Novella–San Marco) run ~5:00 AM–~12:30 AM daily, to ~2:00 AM on Fri and Sat nights; every 4–5 min at peak, 10–12 min early and late. No metro; trams skirt the pedestrian historic centre, which is best walked.
fareInfo: One 90-minute ticket covers tram and Autolinee Toscane buses: €2.00 from 1 Aug 2026 (was €1.70), the same whether bought at stop machines, in the at bus app or by tapping a contactless card or phone on the on-board reader. Validate paper tickets on boarding. 10-ride carnet ~€15.50; no day pass (the Firenze Card+ add-on includes 72 h of transit). The airport tram costs the normal fare.

sights.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
sights.note: A hilltop terrace south of the Arno with a bronze David copy and the classic panorama of the Duomo, bridges and Tuscan hills, busiest at sunset.

sights.name: Uffizi Gallery
sights.note: The Medici's former offices, now one of the world's great art museums, with Botticelli's Birth of Venus and rooms of Leonardo, Raphael and Caravaggio.

sights.name: Florence Cathedral (Duomo) and Brunelleschi's Dome
sights.note: The Gothic cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore and its red-brick dome, climbed by 463 steps to a gallery under the frescoed vault and a rooftop view.
sights.hours: Cathedral Mon–Sat ~10:15 AM–3:45 PM (free); dome climb ~8:15 AM–7:30 PM by timed slot

sights.name: Galleria dell'Accademia
sights.note: Home of Michelangelo's David and his unfinished Prisoners, plus Florentine Gothic paintings and a hall of plaster casts.

sights.name: Mercato Centrale
sights.note: San Lorenzo's 19th-century iron-and-glass market: butchers and produce stalls on the ground floor, a food hall of Tuscan counters upstairs.
sights.hours: Food hall daily ~9:00 AM–12:00 AM; ground-floor market Mon–Sat ~7:00 AM–2:00 PM

sights.name: Piazza della Signoria
sights.note: Florence's civic square, an open-air sculpture gallery with the Neptune Fountain, a copy of David and the Loggia dei Lanzi.

sights.name: Ponte Vecchio
sights.note: The medieval bridge lined with goldsmiths' shops, topped by the Vasari Corridor that linked the Medici palaces.
sights.hours: Bridge always open; shops ~10:00 AM–7:00 PM

sights.name: Basilica of Santa Croce
sights.note: A vast Franciscan church holding the tombs of Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli, Giotto frescoes and Brunelleschi's Pazzi Chapel.

sights.name: Palazzo Vecchio
sights.note: The fortress-like town hall on Piazza della Signoria, with the huge Hall of the Five Hundred, Medici apartments and the Arnolfo tower climb.
sights.hours: Museum ~9:00 AM–7:00 PM daily (Thu to 2:00 PM)

sights.name: Palazzo Pitti and Boboli Gardens
sights.note: The Medici's grand palace across the Arno, with the Palatine Gallery's Raphaels, royal apartments and the terraced Boboli Gardens behind.
sights.hours: Palace Tue–Sun 8:15 AM–6:30 PM; Boboli daily 8:15 AM to dusk (closed 1st and last Mon of month)

sights.name: Basilica di San Miniato al Monte
sights.note: A Romanesque church with a green-and-white marble facade above Piazzale Michelangelo, where monks sing Gregorian vespers at dusk.
sights.hours: ~9:30 AM–1:00 PM and ~3:00–7:00 PM daily; free

sights.name: Giotto's Bell Tower
sights.note: The marble-clad campanile beside the Duomo, 414 steps with no lift, giving the best close-up view of Brunelleschi's dome.

sights.name: Museo Galileo
sights.note: The Medici scientific collection by the Arno: Galileo's telescopes, globes, clocks and instruments, and the scientist's preserved fingers.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–6:00 PM daily, Tue to 1:00 PM

sights.name: Museo Nazionale del Bargello
sights.note: A medieval prison and police headquarters, now Italy's finest Renaissance sculpture museum, with Donatello's bronze David and works by Michelangelo.

sights.name: Medici Chapels
sights.note: The Medici mausoleum behind San Lorenzo: an inlaid-marble Chapel of the Princes and Michelangelo's New Sacristy with his Dawn, Dusk, Night and Day.

sights.name: Basilica of Santa Maria Novella
sights.note: A Dominican church by the main station with an Alberti facade, Masaccio's Trinity and frescoed cloisters.
sights.hours: Mon–Sat ~9:00 AM–5:30 PM (Fri from 11:00 AM), Sun 12:00–5:30 PM

sights.name: Mercato di Sant'Ambrogio
sights.note: A neighbourhood market east of Santa Croce, cheaper and more local than Mercato Centrale, with produce stalls outside and a trattoria inside.

railStations.name: Firenze Santa Maria Novella
railStations.note: Florence's main station on the edge of the old centre: Frecciarossa and Italo high-speed trains to Rome (~1h30m), Bologna (~35 min), Milan (~1h55m) and Venice (~2h10m), plus regional trains to Pisa, Lucca and Siena. Tram T1 (Stazione Alamanni) and T2 (Unità) stop alongside, and the Duomo is a 10-min walk.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:15 AM–~1:30 AM; trains run to individual timetables. Trams ~5:00 AM–~12:30 AM.

airports.name: Florence Airport Peretola
airports.transitNote: Tram T2 (on the map) runs from the stop in front of the terminal to Santa Maria Novella (Unità) in ~20 min and on to San Marco in ~30 min, every 5–10 min, normal fare. Many travellers fly into Pisa (PSA) instead: the PisaMover shuttle and a train reach Santa Maria Novella in ~1h15m (not on the map).
airports.hours: Tram T2: first ~5:00 AM, last ~12:30 AM (~2:00 AM Fri–Sat).
